art/02-aesthetic-theories-deep: Analytic aesthetics offers competing definitions of art (mimesis, expression, formalism, institutional, historical, and cluster theories), each capturing part of its essence yet failing as a complete definition.
art/01-미학: Aesthetics, the philosophical study of beauty, art, and sensory cognition, preserves as equals six major answers (Plato through Adorno) to why humans define beauty and by what criterion.
art/04-아프리카-라틴-총체예술: African aesthetics, exemplified by Yoruba, Akan, Dogon, and griot traditions, treats art, religion, everyday life, and society as essentially inseparable, an integration carried into the diaspora through survival and re-creation.
art/01-case-applications: Mathematical and neuroaesthetic tools (group theory, fractals, Fourier analysis, information theory) are applied precisely to five works from Bach to Stable Diffusion, demonstrating the math-art combination in practice.
art/02-case-applications-2: Five cases spanning Beethoven's late quartets, Cezanne, Joyce, Song dynasty Peach Blossom Spring painting, and Kara Walker apply combination tools to late style, boundary dissolution, Eastern aesthetics, and political boundaries.
art/03-case-applications-3: Five cases (Schoenberg, Rothko, Borges, Pina Bausch, and Hilma af Klint) apply mathematical and neuroaesthetic analysis to boundary dissolution, the unconscious, and mysticism in modern art.
art/04-case-applications-4: Five cases from Wagner's Tristan chord to Kurosawa's Rashomon analyze the dimensions of boundary, medium, perspective, and environment through mathematical, philosophical, and cross-field influence tools.
art/04-비교예술학·매체이론: Comparative arts, media theory, and the Gesamtkunstwerk tradition together explain how music, literature, and visual art remain distinct media yet influence one another and create novelty across fields.
art/02-cross-modal-math-deep: Five mechanisms of cross-field influence (direct combination, style transfer, shared foundation, media integration, and meta-critique) are given mathematical form through tensor products, functors, colimits, and natural transformations.
art/04-digital-AI-aesthetics: Digital and AI media transform aesthetics itself, as new media theory, NFTs, generative models, and algorithmic culture extend Baudrillard's simulacrum and automate cross-field influence in the twenty-first century.
art/05-동서-미학-비교: A five-civilization comparison shows the West alone began from field separation while India, Japan, East Asia, and Africa began from integration, with the digital age now accelerating re-integration everywhere.
art/03-film-VR-AI-integration: Film, games, VR, and AI multimodal generation progressively expand Wagner's Gesamtkunstwerk, each medium adding integration dimensions until cross-field synthesis itself becomes automated in the twenty-first century.
art/01-Wagner-Bauhaus-총체예술: Wagner's organic Gesamtkunstwerk and the Bauhaus school represent two Western forms of field integration (work-based versus institutional), yet both are latecomers relative to non-Western integrated traditions.
art/03-criticism-theories: Criticism theory, from Greenberg's formalism through the Frankfurt School to Foucault and Baudrillard, marks the dimension where aesthetics confronts society, power, and the formation of the canon.
art/03-경극-판소리-동아시아-총체예술: Chinese jingju's multi-field spectacle and Korean pansori's one-person minimal drama embody East Asian total art, grounded in shared aesthetic concepts such as qiyun, shenyun, and the three distances.
art/08-문학토대: Literature's foundations span rhetoric, narrative, and prosody through formalism, structuralism, and postcolonial theory, organized around forks such as mimesis versus linguistic autonomy and national versus world literature.
art/06-음악토대: Music's foundations integrate theory (harmony, rhythm, form), historical styles, Adorno's and Bourdieu's sociology, and cognitive psychology, while acknowledging the note's confinement to European classical music as a self-critique.
art/01-Natya-Shastra-인도-총체예술: The Natya Shastra, composed roughly two millennia before Wagner, systematizes rasa, bhava, and abhinaya as a theory of total art in which drama, dance, music, poetry, and the visual are originally one.
art/03-신경미학: Neuroaesthetics and evolutionary aesthetics together ground aesthetic experience in brain circuits and Pleistocene adaptations, neurologically redefining the classical answers of Kant, Aristotle, and Adorno.
art/04-new-media-convergence: Twenty-first-century media evolve through five stages from film to AI agents, each adding an integration dimension, with multimodal models projecting all art forms into a common latent space.
art/02-가부키-노-총체예술: Japanese noh and kabuki integrate mask, music, dance, and poetry through aesthetic concepts such as yugen, ma, and jo-ha-kyu, forming an independent total-art tradition centuries before Wagner.
art/06-non-western-deep-integration: The five non-Western traditions share a common meta-structure of full field integration practiced since antiquity, revealing that Western field separation and its twelve-tone system are culturally contingent choices.
art/02-예술철학: Late twentieth-century analytic philosophy of art answers what art is through five competing frameworks (Goodman's symbols, Danto's historicism, Dickie's institution, Wollheim's expression, Carroll's narrative), redefining classical aesthetics analytically.
art/05-additional-theories: Seven twenty-first-century theoretical tracks, including new materialism, affect theory, and posthumanism, extend aesthetics into the dimensions of matter, body, environment, and sound beyond digital AI aesthetics.
art/07-africa-latin-deep: African and Latin American aesthetics, from Senghor's Negritude and Yoruba ashe to Garcia Canclini's hybridity, articulate vital force, postcolonial critique, and cultural mixing as full aesthetic systems.
art/05-예술사회학: Sociology of art analyzes art's social determination through Bourdieu's field theory, Becker's art worlds, and Heinich's singularity regime, showing reputation and aesthetic judgment as socially produced.
art/06-spinoza-deleuze-immanence: Spinoza's immanent substance, conatus, and affect, developed through Deleuze's philosophy of difference, provide the common foundation for twenty-first-century affect theory, new materialism, and posthuman aesthetics.
art/07-미술토대: Visual art's foundations combine color, composition, and perspective theory with era styles, art history from Wolfflin to Belting, and visual neuroscience, tracing representation's shift toward abstraction and the digital.
art/01-meta-questions-deep: Three meta-questions (why humans define beauty, by what criteria, and how fields cross-influence) are deepened structurally, showing four explanatory layers operating simultaneously and colliding with the hard problem of consciousness.
